source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 99: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions: this is collective-initialization scenario variant 99; backend, launcher, versions, expected world size, host placement, scheduler, container permissions, fabric, selected interfaces, topology, and exact blocked stage are unknown. Measure them rather than infer them. Use an isolated authorized allocation, redact endpoints and credentials, set a finite watchdog, and guarantee cleanup. First capture a run ID, host/rank/local-rank/world size, PID, software and configuration hashes, rendezvous/store endpoint identifiers (redacted), per-rank process-group and collective entry/exit timestamps, last-progress time, stderr, transport logs, and GPU/NIC identifiers. Verify that every expected rank starts exactly once, membership and rendezvous endpoint agree, all ranks enter collectives in identical order, GPU visibility and rank-to-device mapping are unique, and driver/runtime/backend versions are compatible. Check peer access, PCIe/NVLink topology, container devices, shared memory, ulimits, NIC/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall settings, and the interface selected by the backend. Run a minimal same-dtype all-reduce with a short, explicit timeout before the full workload.

Falsifiable hypothesis: one or more ranks have inconsistent rendezvous membership or a rank-specific selected transport path, so the participants do not enter the same collective. Support it only if repeated matched trials reproduce the same missing/late rank, endpoint mismatch, or path-specific transport error and the symptom disappears when that single factor is corrected. Falsify it if membership, entry order, and path diagnostics are identical while the hang persists, or if changing the suspected path does not change the outcome. Do not claim root cause from a timeout alone.

Controlled experiment: freeze code, image, world size, placement, seed, message size, timeout, and scheduler allocation. Randomize trial order and repeat enough times to report per-trial success, timeout, rank failure, and cleanup denominators. Compare (a) single-node, (b) reduced-world, and (c) full-world runs; then change one factor at a time: explicit interface/address family, rendezvous/store, topology or rank mapping, and backend debug setting. Preserve raw logs and a configuration manifest. Compare all-reduce correctness checksums, initialization latency distributions, progress timestamps, transport errors, and resource/CPU/NIC/GPU telemetry. A healthy result requires every rank to enter and exit, correct output, bounded latency, and no leaked processes; record uncertainty and confidence intervals rather than extrapolating from one run.

Competing explanations include collective-order mismatch, duplicate or absent ranks, stale rendezvous state, firewall/DNS/MTU/route issues, incompatible driver/runtime/backend, GPU visibility or peer-access errors, PCIe/NIC topology problems, resource exhaustion, container limits, scheduler placement, and an application race. Distinguish them with the captured evidence and negative controls. Set a bounded watchdog, terminate only the isolated test allocation, collect diagnostics before cleanup, and use staged rollback: stop full-world rollout if any correctness, rank-completeness, timeout/SLO, or cleanup gate fails. Evidence required before attributing cause: complete per-rank membership/entry timeline, exact versions/configuration, topology and interface data, repeated matched trial table, minimal all-reduce result, and logs showing whether the failure follows a rank or path. This is provisional diagnosis guidance, not proof of platform-specific behavior.
